<style type="text/css">
.sdc-route-page {
  --sdc-black: #06090d;
  --sdc-ink: #10151d;
  --sdc-text: #202832;
  --sdc-muted: #64717e;
  --sdc-line: #dce4ea;
  --sdc-white: #ffffff;
  --sdc-cloud: #f4f7f9;
  --sdc-green: #40b7b4;
  --sdc-blue: #6600cc;
  --sdc-orange: #ec6308;
  --sdc-cyan: #71d6e2;
  --sdc-yellow: #ec6308;
  --sdc-red: #ff5a5f;
  --sdc-radius: 8px;
}

.sdc-route-page,
.sdc-route-page * {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

.sdc-route-page {
  width: 100%;
  max-width: 100%;
  margin: 0;
  overflow: visible;
  color: var(--sdc-text);
  background: #f6fbfc;
  font-family: "Open Sans", Arial, sans-serif;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-shell{
  width: min(1160px, calc(100% - 44px));
  margin: 0 auto;
  position: relative;
  z-index: 2;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero{
  min-height: 100vh;
  display: flex;
  align-items: stretch;
  position: relative;
  overflow: clip;
  background:
    radial-gradient(circle at 16% 18%, rgba(236, 99, 8, .24) 0%, transparent 34%),
    radial-gradient(circle at 88% 12%, rgba(64, 183, 180, .18) 0%, transparent 32%),
    linear-gradient(125deg, #090018 0%, #19003b 42%, #3d007f 72%, #6600cc 100%),
    linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(64, 183, 180, .1) 1px, transparent 1px),
    linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(64, 183, 180, .08) 1px, transparent 1px);
  background-size: auto, auto, auto, 42px 42px, 42px 42px;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 100vmax #090018;
  clip-path: inset(0 -100vmax);
  color: #ffffff;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero::after{
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  height: 10px;
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--sdc-green), var(--sdc-orange), var(--sdc-blue));
}

.sdc-route-page .route-topbar{
  height: 92px;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 18px;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-logo{
  width: min(232px, 58vw);
  height: auto;
  display: block;
  padding: 0;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: transparent;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-topbar__tag,
.sdc-route-page .route-small-title,
.sdc-route-page .selector-progress__text{
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .78rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  text-transform: none;
  letter-spacing: 0;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-topbar__tag{
  color: #ffffff;
  border: 1px solid rgba(64, 183, 180, .5);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, .08);
  padding: 9px 12px;
  border-radius: 999px;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__grid{
  min-height: calc(100vh - 92px);
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(560px, 1.08fr) minmax(320px, .72fr);
  gap: clamp(24px, 4vw, 56px);
  align-items: center;
  padding: 24px 0 72px;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__content{
  width: min(760px, 100%);
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  justify-content: center;
  padding: 0;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-kicker{
  width: fit-content;
  margin: 0 0 18px;
  padding: 7px 11px;
  color: #ffffff;
  background: rgba(236, 99, 8, .95);
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .74rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  text-transform: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero h1,
.sdc-route-page .route-intro h2,
.sdc-route-page .selector-panel h2,
.sdc-route-page .selector-panel h3,
.sdc-route-page .question-stage h2,
.sdc-route-page .result-stage h2{
  margin: 0;
  font-family: "Barlow Semi Condensed", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-weight: 700;
  line-height: 1.02;
  letter-spacing: 0;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero h1{
  max-width: 760px;
  color: #ffffff;
  font-size: clamp(3rem, 4.75vw, 4.95rem);
  text-transform: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__lead{
  max-width: 650px;
  margin: 20px 0 0;
  color: rgba(255, 255, 255, .78);
  font-size: clamp(1rem, 1.6vw, 1.14rem);
  line-height: 1.55;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__steps{
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 10px;
  margin-top: 28px;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__steps article{
  min-height: 132px;
  padding: 14px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(64, 183, 180, .3);
  border-radius: var(--sdc-radius);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, .08);
  box-shadow: 0 18px 42px rgba(0, 0, 0, .22);
  backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__steps strong{
  width: 28px;
  height: 28px;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  margin-bottom: 12px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  color: #ffffff;
  background: var(--sdc-orange);
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .72rem;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__steps span{
  display: block;
  color: #ffffff;
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .84rem;
  font-weight: 800;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__steps small{
  display: block;
  margin-top: 6px;
  color: rgba(255, 255, 255, .68);
  font-size: .82rem;
  line-height: 1.4;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__actions,
.sdc-route-page .selector-actions,
.sdc-route-page .result-actions{
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 12px;
  margin-top: 32px;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-action-note{
  display: block;
  flex-basis: 100%;
  color: rgba(255, 255, 255, .72);
  font-size: .88rem;
  font-weight: 700;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-button{
  min-height: 48px;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 9px;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--sdc-radius);
  padding: 14px 19px;
  color: var(--sdc-black);
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .9rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  text-decoration: none;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: transform .2s ease, background .2s ease, border-color .2s ease;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-button:hover{
  transform: translateY(-2px);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-button--large{
  min-height: 58px;
  padding: 17px 26px;
  font-size: 1rem;
  color: #ffffff;
  background: var(--sdc-orange);
  box-shadow: 7px 7px 0 #25004f;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-button--primary{
  background: var(--sdc-green);
  color: #06232e;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-button--primary.route-button--large{
  background: var(--sdc-orange);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-button--ghost{
  color: #ffffff;
  border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, .2);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, .08);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-button--dark{
  color: var(--sdc-text);
  border-color: var(--sdc-line);
  background: var(--sdc-white);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-hero__media{
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  z-index: 1;
  pointer-events: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-field{
  position: absolute;
  right: clamp(-260px, -8vw, -90px);
  top: 11%;
  width: min(720px, 64vw);
  aspect-ratio: 1.2 / 1;
  border: 2px solid rgba(64, 183, 180, .28);
  transform: rotate(-11deg);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-field::before,
.sdc-route-page .route-field::after,
.sdc-route-page .field-line,
.sdc-route-page .field-node{
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  display: block;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-field::before{
  inset: 12%;
  border: 2px solid rgba(236, 99, 8, .18);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-field::after{
  left: 50%;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  width: 2px;
  background: rgba(64, 183, 180, .2);
}

.sdc-route-page .field-line{
  height: 2px;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, .16);
}

.sdc-route-page .field-line--one{
  left: 7%;
  top: 28%;
  width: 70%;
}

.sdc-route-page .field-line--two{
  left: 25%;
  top: 55%;
  width: 64%;
}

.sdc-route-page .field-line--three{
  left: 11%;
  top: 76%;
  width: 52%;
}

.sdc-route-page .field-node{
  width: 18px;
  height: 18px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--sdc-green);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px rgba(64, 183, 180, .14);
}

.sdc-route-page .field-node--one{ left: 16%; top: 24%; }
.sdc-route-page .field-node--two{ left: 58%; top: 51%; background: var(--sdc-cyan); box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px rgba(32, 184, 255, .14); }
.sdc-route-page .field-node--three{ left: 33%; top: 72%; background: var(--sdc-orange); box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px rgba(236, 99, 8, .16); }
.sdc-route-page .field-node--four{ right: 13%; top: 32%; background: var(--sdc-red); box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px rgba(255, 90, 95, .14); }

.sdc-route-page .route-preview-card{
  position: relative;
  min-height: 440px;
  border: 14px solid #23004e;
  border-radius: 28px;
  background:
    linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(64, 183, 180, .8), rgba(102, 0, 204, .34)),
    linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, .08) 1px, transparent 1px),
    linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, .07) 1px, transparent 1px),
    #15002f;
  background-size: auto, 32px 32px, 32px 32px, auto;
  box-shadow: 20px 28px 0 #2a0057, 0 30px 70px rgba(42, 0, 87, .24);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-preview-card::before{
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  inset: 54px 46px auto auto;
  width: 170px;
  height: 170px;
  border: 2px solid rgba(236, 99, 8, .34);
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 0 34%, rgba(236, 99, 8, .72) 35% 39%, transparent 40%);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-preview-card__counter{

  border-radius: 18px;

  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .82rem;

.sdc-route-page .route-preview-card__screen{

}

.sdc-route-page .route-preview-card__pill{
  display: inline-flex;
  margin-bottom: 10px;
  padding: 5px 8px;

  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .68rem;
  font-weight: 900;
  text-transform: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-preview-card h2{
  margin: 0;
  font-family: "Barlow Semi Condensed", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 3vw, 2.7rem);
  line-height: 1;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-preview-card__title{
  margin: 0;
  color: #ffffff;
  font-family: "Barlow Semi Condensed", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 3vw, 2.7rem);
  font-weight: 700;
  line-height: 1;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-preview-card p{
  margin: 8px 0 0;
  color: rgba(255, 255, 255, .82);
  font-size: .92rem;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-intro{
  padding: 78px 0;
  background: var(--sdc-white);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 100vmax var(--sdc-white);
  clip-path: inset(0 -100vmax);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-intro__grid{
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, .86fr) minmax(320px, .78fr);
  gap: 36px;
  align-items: center;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-small-title{
  display: inline-flex;
  margin-bottom: 14px;
  color: var(--sdc-blue);
}

.sdc-route-page .route-intro h2,
.sdc-route-page .selector-panel h2,
.sdc-route-page .selector-panel h3,
.sdc-route-page .result-stage h2{
  font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 3.2vw, 3.35rem);
  text-transform: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .route-intro__copy{
  position: relative;
  display: grid;
  gap: 14px;
  padding: 28px 30px 28px 82px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(64, 183, 180, .28);
  border-left: 6px solid var(--sdc-green);
  border-radius: var(--sdc-radius);
  background: #f7fcfd;
  box-shadow: 0 18px 42px rgba(64, 183, 180, .1);

.sdc-route-page .route-intro__icon{

  border-radius: 50%;

  background: var(--sdc-orange);
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .82rem;
  font-weight: 900;

.sdc-route-page .route-intro__copy p{

.sdc-route-page .route-selector{

.sdc-route-page .question-stage,
.sdc-route-page .result-stage{
  border: 1px solid var(--sdc-line);
  border-radius: var(--sdc-radius);

}

.sdc-route-page .selector-panel{

  top: auto;

}

.sdc-route-page .question-stage{
  min-height: 500px;
  padding: clamp(22px, 4vw, 42px);
}

.sdc-route-page .question-stage h2{
  color: var(--sdc-ink);
  font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 3.4vw, 3.45rem);
  text-transform: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .question-title{
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--sdc-ink);
  font-family: "Barlow Semi Condensed", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 3.4vw, 3.45rem);
  font-weight: 700;
  line-height: 1.02;
}

.sdc-route-page .answer-grid{
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 12px;
  margin-top: 30px;
}

.sdc-route-page .answer-option{
  min-height: 114px;
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: 13px;
  width: 100%;
  border: 1px solid var(--sdc-line);
  border-radius: var(--sdc-radius);
  padding: 16px;
  text-align: left;
  background: #fbfcfd;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: border-color .2s ease, transform .2s ease, background .2s ease;
}

.sdc-route-page .answer-option:hover,
.sdc-route-page .answer-option.is-selected{
  border-color: var(--sdc-green);
  background: #eefbfb;
  transform: translateY(-2px);
}

.sdc-route-page .answer-option__mark{
  width: 28px;
  min-width: 28px;
  height: 28px;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  border-radius: 50%;
  color: var(--sdc-black);
  background: var(--sdc-green);
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .76rem;
  font-weight: 800;
}

.sdc-route-page .answer-option strong{
  display: block;
  color: var(--sdc-ink);
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .96rem;
  line-height: 1.25;
}

.sdc-route-page .answer-option span:last-child{
  display: block;
  margin-top: 6px;
  color: var(--sdc-muted);
  font-size: .9rem;
  line-height: 1.45;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-stage{
  grid-column: 1 / -1;
  overflow: hidden;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-card{
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(320px, .92fr) minmax(0, 1.08fr);
  min-height: 600px;
  background:
    linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(64, 183, 180, .12), rgba(236, 99, 8, .08)),
    #ffffff;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-card__image{
  min-height: 520px;
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  justify-content: center;
  padding: clamp(18px, 3vw, 34px) clamp(18px, 3vw, 34px) 24px;
  background: #f0fbfc;
  text-decoration: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-card__image img{
  width: 100%;
  max-height: 520px;
  object-fit: contain;
  border-radius: var(--sdc-radius);
  box-shadow: 0 20px 46px rgba(16, 21, 29, .12);
}

.sdc-route-page .result-card__body{
  padding: clamp(24px, 4.5vw, 52px);
}

.sdc-route-page .result-badge{
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  margin-bottom: 16px;
  padding: 8px 11px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  color: #ffffff;
  background: var(--sdc-green);
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .78rem;
  font-weight: 900;
  text-transform: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-stage p{
  color: var(--sdc-muted);
  font-size: 1rem;
  line-height: 1.65;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-details{
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 14px;
  margin: 30px 0 0;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-detail{
  min-height: 210px;
  padding: 18px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(64, 183, 180, .28);
  border-radius: var(--sdc-radius);
  background: #ffffff;
  box-shadow: 0 14px 34px rgba(42, 0, 87, .08);
}

.sdc-route-page .result-detail strong{
  display: block;
  margin: 12px 0 10px;
  color: #071426;
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .95rem;
  line-height: 1.2;
  text-transform: none;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-detail__icon{
  width: 34px;
  height: 34px;
  display: inline-flex !important;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  border-radius: 999px;
  color: #ffffff !important;
  background: var(--sdc-orange);
  font-family: "Montserrat", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: .74rem !important;
  font-weight: 900;
  line-height: 1;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-detail span{
  color: var(--sdc-muted);
  font-size: .91rem;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-actions{
  margin-top: 28px;
}

.sdc-route-page .whatsapp-button{
  background: #25d366;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-actions .route-button{
  color: #ffffff;
}

.sdc-route-page .result-actions .route-button--primary{
  background: var(--sdc-green);
}

.sdc-route-page .result-actions .route-button--dark{
  color: var(--sdc-blue);
  background: #ffffff;
}

.sdc-route-page .is-hidden{
  display: none !important;
}

@media (max-width: 980px) {
  .sdc-route-page .route-hero{
    min-height: 100vh;
  }

  .sdc-route-page .route-topbar{

  }

  .sdc-route-page .route-topbar__tag{

  }

  .sdc-route-page .route-hero__grid{

  .sdc-route-page .answer-grid{

  .sdc-route-page .question-stage,

  position: relative;

  background:

}

.sdc-route-page .route-seo-block::before,
.sdc-route-page .route-seo-block::after {
  content: "";

  pointer-events: none;
  border: 1px solid rgba(64, 183, 180, .18);
  transform: rotate(-8deg);

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  const gallery = document.getElementById("sdcGallery");
  const lightbox = document.getElementById("sdcLightbox");
  const lightboxImg = document.getElementById("sdcLightboxImg");
  const closeBtn = document.getElementById("sdcCloseBtn");
  const prevBtn = document.getElementById("sdcPrevBtn");
  const nextBtn = document.getElementById("sdcNextBtn");

  if (!gallery || !lightbox || !lightboxImg) return;

  /* Mover el lightbox al final del body para evitar problemas de z-index en Divi */
  document.body.appendChild(lightbox);

  const galleryImages = gallery.querySelectorAll(".sdc-gallery-item img");
  if (!galleryImages.length) return;

  let currentIndex = 0;

  function openLightbox(index) {
    currentIndex = index;
    lightboxImg.src = galleryImages[currentIndex].src;
    lightboxImg.alt = galleryImages[currentIndex].alt || "";
    lightbox.classList.add("active");
    lightbox.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "false");
    document.body.style.overflow = "hidden";
  }

  function closeLightbox() {
    lightbox.classList.remove("active");
    lightbox.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
    document.body.style.overflow = "";
  }

  function showNextImage() {
    currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % galleryImages.length;
    lightboxImg.src = galleryImages[currentIndex].src;
    lightboxImg.alt = galleryImages[currentIndex].alt || "";
  }

  function showPrevImage() {
    currentIndex = (currentIndex - 1 + galleryImages.length) % galleryImages.length;
    lightboxImg.src = galleryImages[currentIndex].src;
    lightboxImg.alt = galleryImages[currentIndex].alt || "";
  }

  galleryImages.forEach(function (img, index) {
    img.addEventListener("click", function () {
      openLightbox(index);
    });
  });

  if (closeBtn) {
    closeBtn.addEventListener("click", closeLightbox);
  }

  if (nextBtn) {
    nextBtn.addEventListener("click", showNextImage);
  }

  if (prevBtn) {
    prevBtn.addEventListener("click", showPrevImage);
  }

  lightbox.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
    if (e.target === lightbox) {
      closeLightbox();
    }
  });

  document.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) {
    if (!lightbox.classList.contains("active")) return;

    if (e.key === "Escape") closeLightbox();
    if (e.key === "ArrowRight") showNextImage();
    if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") showPrevImage();
  });
});</script>

											<div class="et_post_meta_wrapper">
							<h1 class="entry-title">Discover the 8 most important football metrics</h1>

						<p class="post-meta"><span class="published">Aug 14, 2026</span></p><img fetchpriority="high" src="https://english-programs.sportsdatacampus.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Discover-the-8-most-important-football-metrics-1080x675.jpeg" alt="Discover the 8 most important football metrics" class="" width="1080" height="675" srcset="https://english-programs.sportsdatacampus.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Discover-the-8-most-important-football-metrics-1080x675.jpeg 1080w, https://english-programs.sportsdatacampus.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Discover-the-8-most-important-football-metrics-980x653.jpeg 980w, https://english-programs.sportsdatacampus.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Discover-the-8-most-important-football-metrics-480x320.jpeg 480w" sizes="(min-width: 0px) and (max-width: 480px) 480px, (min-width: 481px) and (max-width: 980px) 980px, (min-width: 981px) 1080px, 100vw" />
												</div>
				
					<div class="entry-content">
					
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Football metrics measure player and team performance through specific actions on the pitch. <strong>Goals, assists, xG, xA, xG Buildup and xThreat</strong> help assess finishing, chance creation, attacking threat and defensive performance. <strong><a href="https://english-programs.sportsdatacampus.com/msc-data-analytics-football/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=MSC-important-football-metrics" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Understanding what each metric measures makes it easier to interpret</a> what actually happens during a match.</strong></p>



<div style="height:21px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">What are football metrics and how are they different from KPIs?</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Football metrics <strong>turn match data into indicators that help assess player and team performance</strong>. A statistic records a specific event, such as passes, shots or recoveries, while a metric organises and contextualises that data to make it easier to interpret.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A KPI goes one step further by selecting <strong>the indicators that coaching staff consider most relevant to a specific objective</strong>. For example, pass completion percentage is a metric, but it becomes a KPI when a team uses it to assess a midfielder’s ability to retain possession or progress the ball under pressure.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The same applies to defensive actions. Recoveries in the opposition half become more relevant when a playing model prioritises <strong>high pressing and winning the ball back quickly after losing possession</strong>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Understanding the relationship between statistics, football metrics and KPIs prevents figures from being analysed in isolation. <strong>Professional analysis connects each metric with the player’s position, competitive context and the team’s tactical objectives.</strong></p>



<blockquote><strong><span style="font-size: 15pt;">Coaches, analysts and sporting directors interpret this data through metrics to adjust tactics, identify trends and evaluate the effectiveness of a playing model</span></strong></blockquote>



<div style="text-align:center;">

<h4 id="modern-attacking-metrics" class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Modern attacking metrics</strong></h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Modern attacking metrics combine traditional and advanced indicators to analyse finishing, chance creation and attacking threat. <strong>They help assess a player’s influence beyond goals and assists</strong>, showing how they contribute to the team’s overall attacking performance.</p>



<div style="height:13px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h5 id="goals" class="wp-block-heading">Goals</h5>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Goals remain the most direct measure of attacking output, but <strong>the number of goals alone does not fully explain a player’s finishing performance</strong>. To interpret this metric properly, analysts compare goals with the quality and volume of chances a player receives.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A forward who scores frequently from a relatively low number of high-quality chances may show strong finishing efficiency, while another player may record similar goal numbers but require considerably more attempts. <strong>Combining goals with metrics such as xG provides a clearer picture of whether a player is finishing above, below or close to expectation.</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Context also matters. Position, playing time, the team’s attacking style and the areas from which shots are taken can significantly affect goal output. For this reason, professional analysis does not treat goals as an isolated figure, but <strong>as part of a broader assessment of attacking performance and finishing efficiency</strong>.</p>



<div style="height:13px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h5 id="assists" class="wp-block-heading">Assists</h5>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Assists measure the final pass or action that directly leads to a goal and remain one of the clearest indicators of a player’s contribution to chance creation. However, <strong>assist totals depend heavily on whether teammates convert the opportunities created</strong>, so they should not be interpreted in isolation.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Two players may create chances of similar quality but finish the season with very different assist numbers because of differences in finishing. This is why analysts combine assists with metrics such as xA, key passes and chances created to understand <strong>how consistently a player generates valuable opportunities for teammates</strong>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The tactical role also influences this metric. Wingers, attacking midfielders and full-backs may create chances from very different areas and through different actions, from crosses and cut-backs to through balls or set pieces. <strong>Analysing assists alongside the player’s position and creative responsibilities provides a more accurate picture of their attacking contribution.</strong></p>



<div style="height:13px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h5 id="x-g-expected-goals" class="wp-block-heading">Expected Goals (xG)</h5>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Expected Goals (xG) estimates <strong>the probability that a shot will result in a goal based on the characteristics of the chance</strong>. Models usually consider factors such as shot location, angle, body part used and the type of assist or action that created the opportunity.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">An xG value of 0.30 means that similar chances are converted roughly 30% of the time. This allows analysts to distinguish between the final scoreline and the underlying quality of the chances created. <strong>A team can win a match while generating lower-quality opportunities than its opponent, or lose despite producing stronger chances.</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">At player level, comparing goals with xG helps assess finishing over time. A player who regularly scores more than their accumulated xG may be finishing efficiently, while consistently scoring below it can indicate the opposite. <strong>xG is therefore most useful when analysed across a sufficient sample of matches rather than from a single performance.</strong></p>



<div style="height:13px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h5 id="x-a-expected-assists" class="wp-block-heading">Expected Assists (xA)</h5>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Expected Assists (xA) estimates <strong>the probability that a completed pass will become an assist based on the quality of the chance it creates</strong>. It therefore helps measure creative contribution without depending entirely on whether a teammate finishes the opportunity.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A player can record a high xA figure and still finish with few assists if teammates fail to convert the chances created. In the same way, a player may accumulate assists from lower-quality situations that are finished unusually well. <strong>Comparing assists with xA helps separate chance creation from finishing outcomes.</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This metric is especially useful when analysing creative midfielders, wingers and full-backs, although its value depends on tactical role and the areas from which chances are created. <strong>Used alongside key passes, progressive actions and actual assists, xA provides a more complete view of a player’s creative influence.</strong></p>



<div style="height:21px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>

<h4 id="metrics-of-involvement-and-chance-creation" class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Metrics of involvement and chance creation</strong></h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Metrics of involvement and threat creation analyse actions that contribute to the attack before the final pass or shot.</strong> Indicators such as xG Buildup and xThreat help identify which players are involved in attacking build-up, progress the ball and increase the threat to the opposition goal even when they do not record goals or assists.</p>



<div style="height:13px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h5 id="actions-that-create-advantage-x-threat" class="wp-block-heading">xG Buildup</h5>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">xG Buildup measures <strong>a player’s involvement in attacking sequences before the final pass or shot</strong>. It assigns value to players who contribute to the build-up of moves that eventually produce a chance, even when they do not provide the assist or take the shot themselves.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This makes the metric particularly useful for midfielders, full-backs and players who help progress possession through passing, positioning or ball carrying. <strong>A high xG Buildup value can highlight players whose influence is important earlier in attacking moves</strong>, rather than only in the final action.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Its interpretation should always consider the team’s style of play and the player’s tactical role. Possession-dominant teams naturally generate more build-up actions, so <strong>xG Buildup is most useful when analysed alongside progressive passes, carries and overall involvement in possession.</strong></p>



<div style="height:13px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h5 id="attacking-involvement-in-earlier-phases-x-g-buildup" class="wp-block-heading">xThreat</h5>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Expected Threat (xThreat) measures <strong>how much an action increases the attacking threat of a possession based on where the ball moves on the pitch</strong>. Unlike xG, which focuses on shots, xThreat can assign value to passes and carries that move the ball into more dangerous areas.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A progressive pass or carry may therefore generate a high xThreat value even if the move does not immediately end in a shot. <strong>This makes the metric useful for identifying players who consistently move possession into zones where the probability of creating a dangerous attack increases.</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Its interpretation depends on the player’s role and the team’s style of play. Wingers, attacking midfielders and full-backs may generate threat in very different ways. <strong>Used alongside progressive passes, carries and xG Buildup, xThreat helps show how a player contributes to creating danger throughout an attacking sequence.</strong></p>



<div style="height:21px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h4 id="advanced-defensive-metrics" class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Advanced defensive metrics</strong></h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Advanced defensive metrics measure how players disrupt opposition attacks, regain possession and reduce the effectiveness of attacking actions.</strong> Interceptions, recoveries, pressure, duels and blocks provide context beyond tackles alone and help analysts understand a player’s defensive contribution according to their position and tactical role.</p>



<div style="height:13px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h5 id="interceptions-and-recoveries" class="wp-block-heading">Interceptions and recoveries</h5>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Interceptions and recoveries measure <strong>a player’s ability to disrupt opposition possession and help their team regain the ball</strong>. Interceptions usually reflect anticipation and positioning, while recoveries occur when a player takes possession following a loose ball, misplaced pass or defensive action.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">These metrics are particularly useful when analysing defenders and midfielders, but raw totals can be misleading. A player in a team that spends more time without the ball will naturally have more opportunities to record defensive actions. <strong>Possession, defensive structure and pressing intensity therefore need to be considered when comparing players.</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The location of the action also provides valuable context. Winning possession close to the opposition goal can immediately create an attacking opportunity, while a recovery deeper on the pitch may help stop a dangerous move. <strong>Interceptions and recoveries become more useful when analysts consider where possession is regained and what happens next.</strong></p>



<div style="height:13px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h5 id="pressure-duel-success-and-blocks" class="wp-block-heading">Pressure, duel success and blocks</h5>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Pressure, duel success and blocks measure <strong>how effectively a player contests possession, restricts opponents and prevents attacking actions from developing</strong>. Together, they provide a broader view of defensive performance than tackles or interceptions alone.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Pressures show how frequently a player closes down an opponent and attempts to limit their time or passing options. Duel success measures performance in direct contests for possession, while blocks record interventions that stop shots, passes or crosses from reaching their intended target.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">These actions depend heavily on position and playing style. A centre-back, full-back and midfielder will face very different defensive situations, so <strong>their numbers should be interpreted according to tactical role, team structure and the areas of the pitch in which those actions occur.</strong></p>



<div style="height:21px" aria-hidden="true" class="wp-block-spacer"></div>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">How to interpret key football metrics</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Player analysis requires football metrics to be interpreted within the context in which each footballer performs.</strong> A single figure cannot explain performance on its own, as position, tactical role, playing model and competitive level all influence the numbers produced. <strong>To build an accurate assessment, analysts need to connect each metric with the factors that explain how and why that performance occurs</strong>:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li><strong>Position and tactical role</strong>: The same metrics do not carry the same value for a forward, midfielder or centre-back. Analysis should prioritise the indicators most closely related to the responsibilities of each player.</li>



<li><strong>Playing model</strong>: Possession, defensive line height, circulation speed and pressing intensity directly influence the data a player generates. Comparing players without considering these factors can distort the assessment.</li>



<li><strong>Consistency over time</strong>: One outstanding match does not define performance. Analysing a broader sample helps identify patterns, assess the stability of the numbers and distinguish sustained behaviours from isolated performances.</li>



<li><strong>Competitive context</strong>: The level of the league, the quality of the opposition and different match situations affect the difficulty of every action. The same figure can therefore have a different meaning depending on the environment in which it is produced.</li>



<li><strong>Relationship between metrics</strong>: No single indicator provides a complete assessment on its own. Combining attacking output, threat creation, involvement and defensive performance helps build a much more accurate player profile.</li>
</ul>



<blockquote><strong><span style="font-size: 15pt;">The analysis of a footballer gains greater depth when metrics are integrated into a coherent narrative that explains their behaviour, strengths and areas for development. This approach turns data into a tool that helps to understand the complexity of individual performance</span></strong></blockquote>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Data visualisation in football analysis</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Data visualisation transforms football metrics into representations that make performance easier to interpret.</strong> <a href="https://english-programs.sportsdatacampus.com/best-football-data-visuals/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Heat maps, scatter plots, passing maps and other visualisations</a> help identify individual and collective patterns that can be difficult to spot when analysts work with figures alone.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Effective visualisation also helps connect different metrics within the same context.</strong> Analysts can examine where a player creates threat, which areas they use during attacking build-up or how their defensive activity changes throughout a match. Visualisation therefore does not replace football metrics; it adds context and makes it easier to communicate findings to coaching staff.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Working with football data requires analysts to <strong>select the right metrics, interpret them within the context of the game and turn them into useful information for decision-making</strong>. These skills are now central to the work of sports analytics professionals and form a key part of the <a href="https://english-programs.sportsdatacampus.com/msc-data-analytics-football/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=MSC-important-football-metrics"><strong>MSc Data Analytics in Football</strong></a>, which focuses on applying data and technology to performance analysis and decision-making in football.</p>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Which football metrics should be analysed for each playing position?</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Football metrics should be adapted to the responsibilities of each player. For a forward, finishing and threat creation are usually more relevant, while midfielders require greater focus on involvement in build-up and ball progression. For defensive players, recoveries, interceptions, duels and blocks help assess performance without losing sight of the team’s tactical model.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">How many matches are needed to interpret a football metric?</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">As a practical reference, 8 to 15 matches can help identify general trends with greater consistency. For more variable or individual metrics, analysing 20 matches or more is usually more reliable, while a sample of fewer than five matches is generally too small to draw solid conclusions.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">How should football metrics be compared across different leagues or teams?</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Comparing players requires metrics to be interpreted according to competitive level, playing model, position and tactical role. Possession levels and defensive line height can also influence many figures. A reliable comparison therefore needs to normalise the data and consider the circumstances that explain the differences between both player profiles.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">Does a higher football metric always mean better performance?</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">No. A higher value does not automatically indicate better performance. A defender with many recoveries, for example, may simply face more defensive actions because their team spends longer without the ball. Analysts need to connect each figure with tactical context, opportunity volume and the player’s role before turning a statistical difference into a sporting conclusion.</p>

<script type="rocketlazyloadscript" data-rocket-type="text/javascript">
(function () {
  const el = document.getElementById('sdc-countdown');
  if (!el) return;

  function getNextMondayMidnight() {
    const now = new Date();
    const target = new Date(now);
    target.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    const day = now.getDay();           // 0=Dom, 1=Lun, ... 6=Sáb
    const diff = (1 - day + 7) % 7;     // días hasta el próximo lunes
    target.setDate(now.getDate() + diff);
    if (target <= now) target.setDate(target.getDate() + 7);
    return target;
  }

  const pad2  = n => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
  const pad3  = n => String(n).padStart(3, '0'); // estilo 006 días

  let deadline = getNextMondayMidnight();

  function tick() {
    const now = new Date();
    let ms = deadline - now;

    if (ms <= 0) {
      deadline = getNextMondayMidnight();
      ms = deadline - now;
    }

    const totalSec = Math.floor(ms / 1000);
    const days     = Math.floor(totalSec / 86400);
    const hours    = Math.floor((totalSec % 86400) / 3600);
    const minutes  = Math.floor((totalSec % 3600) / 60);
    const seconds  = totalSec % 60;

    // Una sola línea: Días Horas Minutos Segundos
    el.textContent = `${pad3(days)}d ${pad2(hours)}h ${pad2(minutes)}m ${pad2(seconds)}s`;
    // Si prefieres texto completo: usa la línea de abajo y comenta la de arriba.
    // el.textContent = `${pad3(days)} días ${pad2(hours)} horas ${pad2(minutes)} minutos ${pad2(seconds)} segundos`;
  }

  tick();
  setInterval(tick, 1000);
})();

</script>

<script type="rocketlazyloadscript" data-rocket-type="text/javascript">
(function(){
  if(window.__mbdsfCountersInit) return; // evita doble init
  window.__mbdsfCountersInit = true;

  const locale = 'es-ES';
  const formatter = (d)=> new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {
    minimumFractionDigits: d, maximumFractionDigits: d
  });

  const animate = (el)=>{
    const target = parseFloat(el.dataset.target||'0');
    const duration = parseInt(el.dataset.duration||'1200',10);
    const decimals = parseInt(el.dataset.decimals||'0',10);
    const prefix = el.dataset.prefix||'';
    const suffix = el.dataset.suffix||'';
    const reduce = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

    const setVal=(v)=> el.textContent = `${prefix}${formatter(decimals).format(v)}${suffix}`;

    if(reduce || duration<=0){ setVal(target); el.dataset.done='1'; return; }

    let start=null, from=0, diff=target-from;
    const step=(ts)=>{
      if(!start) start=ts;
      const p=Math.min((ts-start)/duration,1);
      const eased=1-Math.pow(1-p,5);
      setVal(from+diff*eased);
      if(p<1) requestAnimationFrame(step);
      else { setVal(target); el.dataset.done='1'; }
    };
    requestAnimationFrame(step);
  };

  const io = new IntersectionObserver((entries)=>{
    entries.forEach(e=>{
      if(e.isIntersecting){
        const v = e.target.querySelector('.value');
        if(v && v.dataset.done!=='1'){ animate(v); }
      }
    });
  },{threshold:0.35, rootMargin:'0px 0px -10% 0px'});

  document.querySelectorAll('.mbdsf-counter').forEach(card=> io.observe(card));
})();



</script>
